            const key = `workshop:${pageKey}:task:${index}`;
            const saved = localStorage.getItem(key);

            if (saved !== null) {
              box.checked = saved === '1';
            }

            box.addEventListener('change', () => {
              localStorage.setItem(key, box.checked ? '1' : '0');
            });
          });

          document.querySelectorAll('.protocol-notes').forEach((field) => {
            const key = `workshop:${pageKey}:note:${field.dataset.noteId}`;
            const saved = localStorage.getItem(key);

            if (saved !== null) {
              field.value = saved;
            }

            field.addEventListener('input', () => {
              localStorage.setItem(key, field.value);
            });
          });
        });
        </script>

# 3 PCR Product check with agarose gel electrophoresis

**Approximate Time:** 2 hours

## Material

### Equipment and tools

- Electrophoresis box with power supply
- Gel casting tray and comb
- Microwave-safe flask or beaker
- UV transilluminator or gel imaging system
- Balance
- Microwave
- 20µl pipette
- Camera or smartphone

### Consumables

- Gloves
- Paper towels
- Parafilm
- 20µl tips

### Reagents

- 1x TAE buffer
- Agarose powder
- DNA stain such as GelRed
- Molecular weight marker (DNA ladder)
- DNA loading dye
- 5 µl PCR product

## Instructions

- [ ] Weigh 1g agarose for 100ml TAE buffer.
- [ ] Add the agarose powder to the buffer in a microwave-safe flask or beaker.
- [ ] Microwave the solution in short bursts, swirling occasionally, until the agarose is completely dissolved and the solution is clear. Be careful not to overheat.
- [ ] Allow the agarose solution to cool slightly, then add the DNA stain. For GelRed, add 10 µL of the 10,000X stock per 100 mL.
- [ ] Gently swirl the solution to mix in the stain.
- [ ] Pour the agarose solution into a gel casting tray, inserting the comb to create sample wells. Allow the gel to solidify for 20-30 minutes.
- [ ] Once solidified, carefully remove the comb and place the gel into the electrophoresis box. Add 1X TAE buffer until the gel is submerged.
- [ ] Load 6 µL of the molecular weight ladder into the first well.
- [ ] Mix 5 µL of one randomly selected PCR sample with 1-2 µL of DNA loading dye, then load the samples into the remaining wells. Include one positive and one negative control per gel.
- [ ] Connect the electrophoresis box to a power supply and run the gel at 120 V for 30 minutes.
- [ ] Visualize the DNA bands using a UV transilluminator.
- [ ] Take a picture of the gel for documentation. Confirm the correct PCR product size.
- [ ] Repeat the gel for other samples of a stripe in case the lane was blank.

# 4 PCR Clean-up

**Approximate Time:** 1.5 hour

## Material

### Equipment and tools

- Hula Mixer (gentle rotator mixer)
- Vortex mixer
- Microfuge
- Timer
- Quantus® fluorometer
- Magnetic stand suitable for 1.5 ml reaction tubes
- Multichannel pipette
- 1000µl pipette
- 200µl pipette
- 20µl pipette
- 2.5µl pipette

### Consumables

- gloves
- 1000µl tips
- 200µl tips
- 20µl tips
- 10µl filter tips
- 1.5ml reaction tubes

### Reagents

- CleanPCR® magnetic beads
- 75% EtOH, freshly prepared from absolute ethanol e.g. 750µl EtOH with 250µl nuclease free H~2~O in a 1.5ml tube.
- nuclease free H~2~O
- Lambda DNA
- QuantiFluor® dsDNA dye

## Instructions

- [ ] Use the multichannel pipette to pool 10µl from each reaction of all stripes in one new stripe. This is done across all 64 samples of the group.
- [ ] Pool all 8 tubes except the positive control in a 1.5ml tube and vortex 20s.
- [ ] Transfer 20µl in a new 1.5ml reaction tube for each participant.
- [ ] Vortex CleanPCR magnetic beads and shake down before opening the lid.
- [ ] Add 36µl CleanPCR® to the 20µl PCR mix.

**Table 3: PCR reaction volumes and corresponding CleanPCR® volumes**

| PCR Reaction Volume (µL) | CleanPCR (µL) |
|-------------------------:|--------------:|
| 10 | 18 |
| 20 | 36 |
| 40 | 72 |
| 50 | 90 |

- [ ] Incubate on the Hula Mixer for 5 minutes. Spin down.
- [ ] Place the plate on a magnetic separation device to magnetize the CleanPCR particles. Incubate at room temperature until the CleanPCR is completely cleared from solution.
- [ ] Aspirate and discard the cleared supernatant. Do not disturb the CleanPCR particles.
- [ ] Add 200µl 75% ethanol to each well.
- [ ] Incubate at room temperature for 1 minute. It is not necessary to resuspend the CleanPCR particles.
- [ ] Aspirate and discard the cleared supernatant. Do not disturb the CleanPCR.
- [ ] Repeat Steps 9-11 for a second 75% ethanol wash step.
- [ ] After the second wash step spin down the empty tube with the beads, put back on the magnetic stand and use a 10µl pipette to discard the remaining supernatant.
- [ ] Leave the plate on the magnetic separation device for 10-15 minutes to air dry the CleanPCR particles. Remove any residue liquid with a pipet.

> **Note:** It is important to dry the CleanPCR particles before elution. Residual ethanol may interfere with downstream applications.

- [ ] Remove the tube from the magnet.
- [ ] Add 30µl nuclease free H~2~O to the tube.
- [ ] Pipet up and down 20 times or vortex for 30 seconds.
- [ ] Incubate at room temperature for 2-3 minutes.
- [ ] Place the tube on the magnet and incubate at room temperature until the beads are completely cleared from the solution.
- [ ] Transfer the cleared supernatant containing purified DNA to a new 1.5ml tube.

# 5 Quantification

**Approximate Time:** 30min

## Material

### Equipment and tools

- Vortex mixer
- Microfuge
- Quantus® fluorometer
- 200µl pipette
- 2.5µl pipette

### Consumables

- Gloves
- 200µl tips
- 10µl filter tips
- 0.5ml clear reaction tube (e.g. Promega® No. E4941, E4942)

### Reagents

- Lambda DNA standard (400ng/µl)
- QuantiFluor® dsDNA dye
- 1µl unknown sample

## Instructions

- [ ] If needed, calibrate the Fluorometer by reading blank and standard as described by the manufacturer.
- [ ] Add 200µl of QuantiFluor ONE dsDNA Dye® to the 0.5ml PCR tube. Protect tube from light!
- [ ] Add 1µl of unknown samples to 200µl of QuantiFluor® ONE dsDNA Dye in 0.5ml PCR tubes. Vortex well, and protect tube from light.
- [ ] Select the ONE DNA protocol on the Quantus® Fluorometer.
- [ ] Enter the volume of the unknown sample (1µl) and desired concentration units.
- [ ] Measure fluorescence of the unknown sample and record the final sample concentration results.
- [ ] Calculate the volume required for 100 fmol. You may use the Promega BioMath Calculator to convert DNA mass to molar quantity. Select **dsDNA: µg to pmol** and enter the DNA fragment length and DNA amount. The COI amplicon with the 9 bp indexed primer has a size of 726 bp (0.73 kb), or approximately 800 bp (0.8 kb) after ligation of the two adaptors.

[Open the Promega BioMath Calculator](https://www.promega.com/resources/tools/biomath/)

![Scan with your smartphone to open the Promega BioMath Calculator.](figures/promega_biomath_qr.png){#fig-promega-biomath width=25%}
